Slicing a range, as some doctests do, is O(1), but the stated assumption covers that.

Each call scans and partitions its k-element input in O(k), so maximally unbalanced pivots yield O(n²) worst-case time; random pivot ranks give expected O(n log n) time for distinct values. Active frames retain lesser/equal/greater partition lists totaling O(k) elements per frame. Their sizes sum to O(n²) for a maximally unbalanced chain, while random balanced partitions have O(n) expected peak retained list storage. Exclude the input and final returned list; intermediate partition/return lists remain auxiliary.

Owner-reviewed time and auxiliary-space rationale: The exact runtime is O(V² + E log(E+1)): up to V processed vertices each scan a full matrix row, and up to E successful relaxations create heap entries with O(log(E+1)) push/pop cost. Printing adds O(V), dominated. With n=V+E the correct coarse time class is O(n²), tight for sparse connected graphs; O(n log n) would miss the V² scan cost. The returned distances array is output; processed flags use O(V) and lazy duplicate heap entries use O(E), so auxiliary space is O(V+E), coarse O(n).

Time: The method initializes A+1 entries, then for each of A positive amounts scans all C coin denominations. Time is O(A*C + A); for A,C≤n this is O(n²). Auxiliary space: The single minimumCoins array has A+1 integer entries, so auxiliary space is O(A), bounded by O(n). Owner review: The DP array initialization costs O(A); the nested amount/coin loops cost O(A·C), so time is O(A·C). The single A+1-entry array gives O(A) auxiliary space. Under n=max(A,C), the coarse classes O(n²) time and O(n) space are valid. These bounds are pseudo-polynomial in numeric amount A.

Time: The loop compares items in order and may inspect every element when the target is absent or last. Each iteration does constant work. Auxiliary space: The loop stores only the current index and item reference. Owner review: The iterative linear_search compares items until a match or the end. Its worst case examines all n elements, giving O(n) time, and it stores only the current index/item reference, giving O(1) auxiliary space. The recursive helper is outside the reviewed entrypoint.
